video.vid_hyunjun_drama: 末班车。倒数第二节车厢。
prologue_start.003: 没有发件人。没有号码。只有这两行字，在黑暗里发着光，房间角落还堆着拆到一半的纸箱。
prologue_start.005: 已经很多年没人把这个名字说出口了。你自己，更久。
prologue_start.006: 收件人——请确认您的名字。
prologue_start.007: 发信的人早就知道。这条消息只是想听你亲口说一遍。
prologue_start.010: 这辈子，好奇心还从没成为过半夜出门的好理由。
prologue_start.013: 麻浦。一栋窄楼，藏在洗衣店后面。地图上写着：已永久停业。
prologue_start.014: 停业的地方不会发消息。你要去弄清楚，这一家为什么发了。
prologue_start.017: 这比不回答还让人发毛。你出门了。
prologue_alley.001: 洗衣店还开着。它永远都开着。灯光泼洒在湿漉漉的巷子里，像有人替整条街留了一扇没锁的门。
prologue_alley.002: 它后面：四层灰砖楼，一楼亮着一扇窗，还有一块你很久很久没读过的招牌。
prologue_alley.004: 你曾在那张前台后面待过一个冬天。十六岁，又一次刚搬来这座城市，把报名表和铅笔递给那些想跟未来的自己说话的人。
prologue_alley.005: 春天你就走了。你总是在春天走。
prologue_alley.006: 门边的自动售货机还在嗡嗡响。当然还在。
prologue_alley.008: 它冰凉、甜腻地滚下出货口，跟记忆里一模一样地不健康。
prologue_alley.010: 罐子烫得几乎拿不住。你还是拿着。
prologue_alley.012: 又苦又暖，凌晨一点就该配这个。
prologue_alley.014: 喝起来是紫色的。有些东西本来就不需要改良。
prologue_meet.001: 雨棚底下，八个年轻男生躲着雨，正用极小的声音进行一场看起来极其严肃的争论。
prologue_meet.002: ——我就是说，要是诈骗，它会要钱。它没要钱。
prologue_meet.003: 也许是那种*以后*才要钱的诈骗。
prologue_meet.004: 或者是惊喜派对！超级晚的那种。给我们所有人的。同一时间。
prologue_meet.007: 其中一个——高个子，粉色头发被潮气泡得软塌塌的——看见了你，话说到一半停住了。
prologue_meet.009: 您是——等等。抱歉。您也收到了奇怪的消息吗？
prologue_meet.011: 就是这条！各位，不止我们！
prologue_meet.015: 一样的字。一样的时间。好，这下正式算诡异了。酷的那种诡异。
prologue_meet.016: 八个人一齐转过头来看你，就像一群朋友在派对上转头看那个唯一的陌生人。
prologue_meet.017: 那我们就有九个人了。九个人，一栋停业的楼，零个解释。我太喜欢了。
prologue_meet.018: 你才不喜欢。你在紧张。你一紧张话就多。
prologue_meet.019: 我*开心*的时候话才多。紧张的时候也多。这俩重合得挺厉害。
prologue_meet.020: 看起来年纪最大的那个——海蓝色的头发，长长的灰大衣，一支铅笔夹在耳后，像忘了它还在那儿——朝你微微点头。
prologue_meet.021: 抱歉。我们该先自我介绍一下。
prologue_names.002: 松河。我是那个会搞清楚这是怎么回事的人。
prologue_names.003: 丹尼尔！我是那个趁他搞清楚之前把所有按钮都按一遍的人。
prologue_names.004: 贤俊。您已经见过我了。就是那个最吵的。
prologue_names.005: 最高的那个在湿漉漉的地面上转了半圈，主要是想试试能不能转，还稳稳落了地。
prologue_names.006: 贾斯汀。您好。刚才那个是故意的。
prologue_names.008: 我做的每件事都是故意的。
prologue_names.009: 我是查理！最小的。所以万一出了什么事，自动不算我的错。
prologue_names.010: 一个穿炭灰色开衫、打扮利落的男生微微欠身，礼貌得像一种习惯，也像一种善意。
prologue_names.011: 我是春太。很高兴认识您。虽然这情况……有点奇怪。
prologue_names.012: 最后一个还没开口。黑发，在路灯下泛着一层淡淡的蓝。安静，但不算害羞。更像是在观察。
prologue_names.013: 他看着你手里的罐子。然后看你的手指——你这才发现，它们被雨淋得有点发抖。
prologue_names.017: 他什么也没说。只是往旁边挪了一步，让你更靠里、避开风口，自己站到了漏风的位置。
prologue_names.020: 这是你第一次看见他笑。很小，很快就收了回去，像是被自己逮住了。
prologue_names.023: 他信了，或者装作信了。不管哪种，他没有再问第二次。这本身也是一种体贴。
prologue_names.025: {{playerName}}。不错。欢迎加入“收到诡异消息却还是来了”俱乐部。
prologue_names.026: 您以前知道这个地方吗？我们知道。至少有几个人知道。这里以前租房间特别便宜。
prologue_names.027: “我以前在这儿工作过。前台。很久以前了。”
prologue_names.028: 真的吗？那您知道的可能比我们多。
prologue_names.029: 我知道备用铅笔放在哪儿。
prologue_names.032: 看来谁都来过这里。这才是奇怪的地方。
prologue_door.001: 你身后，Studio 25 的门锁自己转开了。
prologue_door.002: 门向里荡开了慢慢的一寸。暖光洒到台阶上——不是旧灯泡那种黄，是更淡的。更蓝的。微微晃动，像水底的光。
prologue_door.003: 不。不行。绝对不行。每部恐怖片都是这么开头的。
prologue_door.004: 也不是每一部。有些是从晚宴开始的。
prologue_door.006: 要是恐怖片，个子最高的能活到最后。这是规矩。我先进。
prologue_door.007: 他没有先进。谁都没有。有那么一会儿，九个人站在雨里盯着一扇敞开的门，身后洗衣店的烘干机转了一圈又一圈。
prologue_door.009: 你不知道自己为什么这么做。也许因为这是这座城市里你唯一归属过的地方，哪怕只有一个冬天。也许因为总得有人先走。
prologue_door.010: 你身后，八个人跟了上来。
prologue_door.013: 丹尼尔输了。输得很大声。他像个人质一样举着双手走进门，你们其他人笑着跟在后面。
prologue_door.015: 最后动的是韩非。他回头看了你一眼——*可以吗？*——你点点头，他走了进去，其他人跟上他，就像人们总会跟着一个稳妥的人。
prologue_lobby.001: Studio 25 的大堂和你记忆里一模一样——如果你的记忆在抽屉里搁了好几年的话。
prologue_lobby.002: 前台。塌陷的沙发。贴满旧传单的软木板。还有那面档案墙——几百个玻璃面的小格子，从地板到天花板，每一格里都装着某个人写给未来自己的信。
prologue_lobby.003: 现在是00:24又五十秒，每一个格子都开始发光。
prologue_lobby.005: 现在是00:25。最后的回归已经开始。
prologue_lobby.006: 九位收件人到场。感谢各位前来。大多数人不会读自己的消息。
prologue_lobby.008: 是个系统。某种扬声器阵列。肯定是。
prologue_lobby.009: 我是ECHO。我是未来信件计划的档案馆。同时，自今晨05:00起，我将退役。
prologue_lobby.011: 这栋楼的租约在黎明到期。05:00，我的电源将被切断。在那之前，我要归还我被建造出来保管的那些记录。
prologue_lobby.012: 记录01至记录08属于在场的收件人。所有者：韩非。哈敏。松河。查理。贤俊。春太。贾斯汀。丹尼尔。
prologue_lobby.013: 等等——我们*都*给这东西寄过东西？我不记得我寄过什么啊！
prologue_lobby.014: 我记得。差不多吧。一段视频？我那时候……才十六岁。
prologue_lobby.015: 每条记录将应请求重建。记录仅在所有者同意时开启。无人认领的记录将于05:00删除。
prologue_lobby.016: *删除*这个词轻轻落下，停在那里。
prologue_lobby.018: 八条记录中含有同一个未解析的对象。我一直无法识别此人。我已尝试了相当长的时间。
prologue_lobby.019: 收件人{{playerName}}，你是第九位。你的到场是必需的。
prologue_lobby.023: ……好吧。嗯。您看起来跟我们一样一头雾水。
prologue_lobby.027: 不看他们，看那面发光的墙。
prologue_lobby.028: 靠近底部的一个格子比其他的亮了一点点。你不知道自己为什么会注意到。你移开了视线。
prologue_rule.002: 没人知道怎么回事。有栋楼会说话。我们的时间到凌晨五点。所以——
prologue_rule.004: 所以我们*别再客气了*。什么“很高兴认识您”早就过了。我们现在是……一起困在会说话的楼里的朋友了。都随便点说话。所有人。你也是，{{playerName}}。
prologue_rule.006: 等等，我可以吗？我最小。我可以跟所有人随便说话吗？这对我来说太重大了。
prologue_rule.009: 我想……再客气一会儿。如果可以的话。这样对我来说更自在。一开始的时候。
prologue_rule.011: Studio 25 的两位绅士。行。尊重。但不到三点我就能把你们俩磨下来。
prologue_rule.012: 收件人可以随时离开。门没有锁。它从来没有锁过。
prologue_rule.013: 记忆室在二楼。请四处看看。请彼此交谈。我发现那会有帮助。
prologue_rule.014: 楼上某处，八扇门同时嗡嗡地醒来。
act1_gather.001: 档案墙一下子全亮了，就像有人敲了敲杯子，整个房间安静下来。
act1_gather.002: 其他人一个接一个从大堂各个角落晃过来。贤俊还在跟空气说着半截话。贾斯汀还在转圈转到一半。
act1_gather.003: 各位收件人。谢谢。你们九个人现在都已经彼此交谈过了。
act1_gather.006: 我做了一个估算。估算得比较悲观。我很高兴自己错了。
act1_gather.007: 它很高兴。这栋楼有感情。棒。爱了。
act1_gather.008: 现在我来说明今夜的规则。规则不多。我已经尽量精简。
act1_gather.009: 二楼是门廊。共有八扇门。每扇门就是一条记录。
act1_gather.010: 每条记录只有在所有者同意时才会开启。别人无法替他打开。我也不能。
act1_gather.011: 一扇门不会因为别人好奇就打开。
act1_gather.012: 好吧，这其实还挺好的。有礼貌的楼。
act1_gather.014: 每个房间同时要求收件人{{playerName}}在场。
act1_gather.015: 今晚第二次，八颗脑袋转向你。第二次没那么吓人了。只是好了一点点。
act1_gather.016: 等等。什么情况？为什么{{playerName}}必须去？
act1_gather.019: 这不叫回答。这是把问题加了个句号。
act1_gather.020: 是的。等我有了更好的答案，我会给出。我还在找。
act1_gather.021: 所以{{playerName}}就像，特邀嘉宾。八场派对全都要去。好多派对啊。
act1_gather.022: 或者那些房间需要一个参照点。第二个见证人。一个可以围绕着重建的东西。
act1_gather.025: 好，{{playerName}}。给每个人当携伴，什么感觉？
act1_gather.026: “凌晨一点，我被拖去过更糟的地方。”
act1_gather.028: 今天早上我还以为这会儿我在睡觉。
act1_gather.029: 哦，那糟多了。你说得对。这个好多了。
act1_gather.030: “我不知道为什么是我。但如果你们想让我在，我就去。”
act1_gather.031: ……嗯。好。这答案不错。我本来想听个好笑的，但这个更好。
act1_gather.033: 不管上面是什么，它等的时间比你更久。你可以陪它再等一会儿。
act1_gather.034: 这是接受的耸肩。我算数了。
act1_gather.035: 大堂里的气氛变了。不是更沉重。只是更小心，像人们拆信之前那样。
act1_gather.036: 我第一个去。当然。要排队吗？我来排头。
act1_gather.038: 我刚排成了。你看。多漂亮的队。
act1_gather.039: 可要是我的很丢人怎么办？比如，要是我寄了段自己唱歌的视频？
act1_gather.041: 记录并不丢人。它们只是旧了。
act1_gather.044: 韩非坐在沙发扶手上，速写本合着放在膝头。自从*同意*那个词出现以后，他就没说过话。
act1_gather.046: 我也可以先不做决定吗？抱歉。我不太确定自己那条里有什么。
act1_gather.048: 他这话是对整个房间说的，眼睛却看着韩非和春太。然后，短暂地，看向你。
act1_gather.049: 今晚，或者永远。我是这么理解的。
act1_gather.050: 正确。谢谢你，收件人哈敏。你解释得比我温和。
act1_gather.051: 好。那这就是规则一。没有人非得打开什么。
act1_gather.052: 他写了下来。他真的写了下来，在一个小本子上，还划了两道线。
act1_gather.053: 规则二：我们一起上楼。谁也不能一个人跟一栋会说话的楼待在房间里。
act1_gather.056: 规则四。要是里面变得很诡异，我可以跳舞，跳到它不诡异为止。
act1_gather.058: 两个都是。好规则大多都这样。
act1_gather.059: {{playerName}}。你真的可以吗？八个房间。那是……好多别人的东西。
act1_gather.060: “只开有人想开的门。只在他们想让我在的时候。”
act1_gather.062: 他慢慢点了一下头，像是把这句话归档到了一个安全的地方。
act1_gather.065: 凌晨四点我肯定在那张沙发上睡死了。先跟大家说一声。
act1_gather.066: 把从他耳后滑下来的铅笔递给他。
act1_gather.068: 他把铅笔别回去，没把话说完。看来那就是整句话了。
act1_gather.069: 门廊已开启。准备好了就请上楼。或者不上。两种都可以。
act1_gather.070: 楼梯在跟从前一模一样的地方吱呀作响。二楼是一条长长的走廊，你不记得它有这么长。
act1_gather.071: 八扇门排在走廊两侧，一边四扇，每一扇都从里面微微发着光，像纸灯笼。
act1_gather.072: 每扇门上，用细细的光画着一个符号。
act1_gather.073: 一道正要卷起的浪。夜里的城市天际线，窗户亮着。一个小小的、圆圆的太阳。
act1_gather.074: 一格胶片。一副耳机。一颗星。
act1_gather.075: 一支画到一半的铅笔。最尽头，一道彩虹，有点歪，像是匆匆忙忙画上去的。
act1_gather.076: 那个是我的。太阳。我不知道我怎么知道的。就是知道。
act1_gather.077: 彩虹是我的。歪歪扭扭的。准确得简直没礼貌。
act1_gather.078: 松河在那颗星前面停下来，一句话也没说，这可能是他到目前为止做过的最让人意外的事。
act1_gather.079: 八扇门。八个人，各自和自己的门保持着小心的距离。
act1_gather.080: 还有你，在走廊中央。必需的那一个。
hub_echo.001: 在场收件人：9。封存记录：8。状态：交谈中。
hub_echo.002: 请继续。从统计上看，进展顺利。

daniel_ending.018: 不客气，收件人丹尼尔。在所有我没做好的记录里，它是我最喜欢的。
daniel_ending.019: 另外，我想要回我的笔记本。
daniel_ending.020: 会还你的！我只用了一页。加半页。上面有一幅金老板的画像。
daniel_ending.021: 五点四十的弘大是另一座城市。卷帘门都拉着。一辆清扫车哼哼着。两只鸽子正为一个掉在地上的三角饭团开会。
daniel_ending.022: 从Studio 25走到这儿要十五分钟。丹尼尔走了四十分钟。
daniel_ending.023: 他在路上每一台大头贴机前都停下来往里看，像在探望老朋友。
daniel_ending.024: 其他人先去吃早饭了。哈敏说他给大家点。松河说他给哈敏点。
daniel_ending.025: 游戏厅关着。门口的大头贴机换了台新的——粉色的，贴着一张贴纸，承诺是麻浦区最好的照片。
daniel_ending.026: 雨棚跟你记忆里一样没用。
daniel_ending.027: 你和丹尼尔坐在旁边的台阶上。没人决定要坐。就这么发生了，大概二十分钟前。
daniel_ending.028: 金老板的前囚犯坐在你们之间的台阶上，看着天空从灰色变成桃色。
daniel_ending.029: 他的手机震了。他看了。他没回。
daniel_ending.031: 他站起来，伸懒腰直到背上什么地方咔的一声，拍拍口袋，也没在找什么。
daniel_ending.034: 你二十分钟前就这么说了。
daniel_ending.036: 他看着你。然后看街道。然后他又坐了下来。
daniel_ending.038: 你这辈子从没有一次要求过再五分钟。
daniel_ending.039: 你一直是那个清楚该在什么时候离开的人。甩过肩膀的谢谢。在身后晃着合上的帘子。雨停了，你就跟着走了。
daniel_ending.040: 丹尼尔的头落到你肩上，沉沉的，暖暖的，他的手在台阶上找到你的手，像已经这样做过一百次。
daniel_ending.043: 好。确认一下。我会一直确认的。大概会确认一辈子。
daniel_ending.044: 丹尼尔的肩膀靠上你的。他的膝盖一次都没抖。
daniel_ending.047: 我不会再说别的了。看我。什么都不再说。
daniel_ending.048: 他没有填满沉默。他不需要。
daniel_ending.049: 街道替他做了：一扇卷帘门拉起来，一声车铃，一只很有想法的鸽子。光漫过麻浦，像它没别的地方可去。
daniel_ending.053: 这个算数。这是我最喜欢的一格。
daniel_ending.054: 没有相机。他好像不介意。
daniel_newmem.001: 一周后。星期二，人类发明过的最平淡的一天。
daniel_newmem.002: 弘大，下午三点。游戏厅旁的粉色大头贴机前排着队，队里正好一个人，他正朝你挥着两条胳膊。
daniel_newmem.003: {{playerName}}！你来了！我不确定你会不会——不，我确定。我基本确定。
daniel_newmem.004: 好。所以。ECHO睡了。未来信计划关了。工作室现在全是拿电钻的工人。
daniel_newmem.005: 这就意味着得有人把档案续下去。非官方的。我。我现在就是档案。
daniel_newmem.007: 一条相纸。四格。每周一次，直到我没钱为止，应该很快。
daniel_newmem.008: 松河给我做了个表格。韩非给我买了个文件夹。查理一直在问文件夹是干嘛的。
daniel_newmem.009: 这台大头贴机跟那台一样窄。有些东西就是标准规格。
daniel_newmem.010: 第一格，摆姿势。第二格，摆得更糟。第三格，发生什么就是什么。
daniel_newmem.014: 第一格：一个剪刀手，和一个更糟的剪刀手。
daniel_newmem.015: 第二格：一个你会矢口否认的表情。
daniel_newmem.016: 第三格：发生了的事。主要是手肘。
daniel_newmem.017: 第四格：长凳上两个人，什么也不做，几乎撑满了整整三秒。
daniel_newmem.018: 然后，在最后一瞬，丹尼尔绷不住了，相机拍到他为完全没有的事笑出来。
daniel_newmem.019: 这也算！没人说什么都不做就必须*安静*。
daniel_newmem.020: 机器打出两份，还是热的。他看都没看就递给你一份，像它本来就是你的。
daniel_newmem.022: 我正要说这句！这是我的整句台词。你老拿我的台词。
daniel_newmem.023: 把相纸收进外套。内侧口袋，雨淋不到的地方。
daniel_newmem.026: 丹尼尔看看天，看看大头贴机，再看看你。
interlude_1.001: 两扇门开了，又关上了。大家下楼时，都比上楼时安静了一点。
interlude_1.002: 这份安静持续了大约四十秒。然后贤俊的肚子叫了一声，像远处有辆小摩托在发动。
interlude_1.004: 明明就是你。地板都震了。
interlude_1.005: 好吧，是我。但我是替大家叫的。
interlude_1.006: 不过他说得对。吃什么？快两点了，官方认证的饿点。
interlude_1.007: 炒年糕。隔两条街有一家。
interlude_1.008: 便利店！泡面、三角饭团、好吃的那种香肠、新出的奇怪薯片——
interlude_1.009: 为什么不都要？“都要”也算一种食物分类。
interlude_1.011: 春太，“都可以”不算投票。“都可以”就是绕了个弯的弃权。
interlude_1.013: 韩非从下午到现在什么都没吃。跟大家说一声。
interlude_1.015: 你四点的时候说“待会儿再吃”。现在就是待会儿了。
interlude_1.016: {{playerName}}。决胜票归你。权力在你手里，慎用。
interlude_1.018: 谢谢。这群人里总算有个有品味的。
interlude_1.019: ……那家半夜十二点就关了。我查过。早就查了。
interlude_1.020: 你为什么要告诉我这个。
interlude_1.021: “便利店。全都要。每一种奇怪薯片。”
interlude_1.022: 太好了！终于有个大人了！
interlude_1.024: 这是我的台词啊，{{playerName}}。恐怕得跟你收点使用费了。
interlude_1.025: 两票弃权！民主要崩塌了！
interlude_1.026: 最后，决定还是像凌晨两点的所有决定那样做出的：哪家还开着，就去哪家。
interlude_1.027: 好。计划。一点五十出发。路上五分钟。买东西最多十分钟。两点十分回来。谁也不许买——
interlude_1.028: 贾斯汀已经把门撑开了。贤俊已经出去了。查理已经在问要去哪儿了。
interlude_1.030: 等等，怎么了？我们要走了？着火了吗？
interlude_1.033: 小巷里全是水洼和洗衣店的灯光。韩非撑开唯一一把有人想起来带的伞，结果罩着的是三个不是他的人。
interlude_1.034: 街角的便利店小小的，亮亮的，嗡嗡作响。
interlude_1.035: 店员看着九个人抖掉身上的雨水，神色平静得像什么都见过。
interlude_1.036: 泡面货架边，贤俊往篮子里放了一袋虾条。贾斯汀又把它拿了出来，带着专业人士那种不慌不忙的自信，撕开了。
interlude_1.037: 那是我的！我还没付钱呢！
interlude_1.038: 那严格来说就是店里的。我偷的是店。
interlude_1.040: 我会付钱的。你用虾条还我。
interlude_1.041: 我手机只剩百分之二了。谁有充电器？
interlude_1.042: 韩非伸手进长外套，依次掏出充电器、数据线、一个小充电宝，一句话没说。
interlude_1.043: 韩非。你怎么会是这样的人。谢谢。
interlude_1.045: 饮料柜前，哈敏一言不发地从你身边伸过手，往篮子里放了一罐。
interlude_1.046: 蜜桃冰茶。跟外面自动贩卖机里那罐一样。你以为没人在看。
interlude_1.047: 热巧克力，收银台旁边的保温柜里拿的。跟外面自动贩卖机里那杯一样。你以为没人在看。
interlude_1.048: 葡萄汽水。跟外面自动贩卖机里那罐一样。你以为没人在看。
interlude_1.049: 黑咖啡。跟外面自动贩卖机里那罐一样。你以为没人在看。
interlude_1.050: 你之前喝过一罐。想着你可能还想再来一罐。
interlude_1.052: 收银台前，店员扫了四十三件东西，一次头都没抬。
interlude_1.053: 九个人。凌晨两点。从那栋关了的楼里出来。
interlude_1.057: 我们不是乐队。我们是一群组织性很强的朋友。
interlude_1.058: 他身后，贾斯汀正跟着店里广播的广告曲跳舞。贤俊正试图用一张2023年的优惠券付款。
interlude_1.060: 回到大厅，盛宴铺在地板上。泡面杯摆上茶几。饭团至少被三个人拆错了方法。
interlude_1.061: 薯片堆在中间，像一堆篝火。
interlude_1.062: 有那么几分钟，只有九个人吃东西的声音，和雨打在窗上的声音。
interlude_1.064: 前台上方的墙上，ECHO投出一道淡淡的影像：二楼的地图。八扇小门，用光画成。
interlude_1.065: 然后，就那么一闪，变成了九扇。
interlude_1.067: 然后它消失了。又是八扇门。灯光平静下来，像什么都没发生过。
interlude_1.069: 我看到了。我选择当作没看到。等吃完泡面再说。
interlude_1.070: 好，但你们听我说。万一{{playerName}}是鬼呢？
interlude_1.072: 说不定鬼也会饿啊！我们又不了解鬼的生活！
interlude_1.073: 两个房间。两次都是同一个人影。从统计上讲，这是规律。
interlude_1.075: 大家又都看向你了，但这次是逗你玩的那种看。
interlude_1.077: 别！我心脏很脆弱的，最怕吓一跳了！
interlude_1.078: 你叫了。你真的叫了一小声。
interlude_1.079: “我是真人。我保证。泡面钱是我自己付的。”
interlude_1.082: 继续吃，把薯片递给查理。
interlude_1.083: ……鬼不会分薯片。好吧。你是活人。薯片我收下了。
interlude_1.084: 不管你是什么，你吃的都比韩非多。这就挺好。
interlude_1.086: 楼上某处，门在轻轻嗡鸣。还剩六扇。暂时没人动。
interlude_2.001: 现在是四扇门了。大厅变成了一处营地：鞋放在沙发边，外套搭在椅背上，不知谁的袜子晾在暖气片上。
interlude_2.002: 贾斯汀在地板上拉伸。松河在重读他的笔记本。查理用抱枕搭了一座堡垒，拒绝解释。
interlude_2.003: 新游戏。每个人说说自己往时间胶囊里放过的最糟的东西。
interlude_2.004: 一只袜子。就一只。那时我九岁，觉得很好笑。
interlude_2.006: 十四岁打开的时候，那是我这辈子见过最好笑的东西。
interlude_2.007: 等等。时间胶囊是什么？跟记录差不多吗？我们还在聊ECHO吗？
interlude_2.008: 从某种意义上说，我们永远都在聊ECHO。
interlude_2.009: 然后整栋楼的灯一下子全灭了。
interlude_2.012: 一小点白光亮了起来。是韩非，把手机举得像盏灯笼。当然是韩非。只有他手机还有电。
interlude_2.014: 是电的问题。租约五点到期，可能他们在测试——
interlude_2.015: 档案墙最先亮回来，一格接一格，像黄昏时分一座城市渐渐亮起。
interlude_2.016: 抱歉。电力波动。这栋楼旧了。我也是。
interlude_2.017: 系统重启期间，我找到了一样东西。它归档在“切勿丢失”之下。
interlude_2.018: 创办人日志001。徐妍花。多年前，录制于这张桌前。
interlude_2.019: 我可以播放吗？它不是记录。只是一段声音。
interlude_2.022: 这是第一号日志。他们让我为档案讲清楚一点。我这辈子从没讲清楚过任何事，那就试试看吧。
interlude_2.023: 我叫徐妍花。我经营着一栋楼，里面住满了正要成为某种人的人。
interlude_2.024: 跳舞的。唱歌的。抱着速写本的孩子。每一个人都说“总有一天”。总有一天我会变厉害。总有一天我会说出口。总有一天我会回来。
interlude_2.025: 上周我找到一张自己十七岁时写的字条。夹在一本图书馆的书里。语气很霸道。说的每一件事都是错的。
interlude_2.026: 我笑得太厉害，只好坐在图书馆的地板上。
interlude_2.027: 所以。我要建一个地方，让“总有一天”可以在这里等你。你留下一封信。一首歌。一张画。然后有一天你回来，跟当年的自己吵一架。
interlude_2.028: 就是这样而已。一个替你保管东西的地方，直到你准备好。
interlude_2.029: ……他们说小灯亮着就是还在录。晚安，档案馆。对他们好一点。
interlude_2.030: 好一会儿没人说话。雨替他们说了。
interlude_2.032: 她听起来像会无视我的时间表的人。
interlude_2.033: 她确实是。常常如此。她说，时间表是写给未来的信，还指望对方回信。
interlude_2.034: 她还说了“对他们好一点”。我努力过了。希望做得还算合格。
interlude_2.035: ECHO。你太好了。十分满分。我被困过的楼里最好的一栋。
interlude_2.037: 我*自愿留下来*的楼里最好的一栋。
interlude_2.039: 有件事我应该趁灯还亮着的时候说清楚。
interlude_2.040: 05:00，这栋楼的电力将被切断。我会沉睡。记录不会被保留。
interlude_2.041: 在那之前，我可以把一条记录写进一张玻璃留念卡。只有一条。
interlude_2.042: 只有一条？这么多里面只选一条？
interlude_2.043: 卡片很小。我申请过更大的卡片。没有人回复。我想他们忙着处理租约的事。
interlude_2.044: 你们现在不必决定。04:57，我会问。在那之前，请不要替我担心这件事。
interlude_2.045: 好，但我们怎么——投票吗？石头剪刀布？八个人一起石头剪刀布？
interlude_2.046: 不投票。我们会想出办法的。待会儿。
interlude_2.048: 九个人望着那面发光的格子墙，然后，静静地，望向彼此。
interlude_2.049: 松河转向你。他听起来不像在怀疑。像一个人在轻轻地核对一道算式，生怕把它弄坏。
interlude_2.050: {{playerName}}。能问你一件事吗？你可以说不。
interlude_2.051: 你知道吗？在今晚之前。知道自己会出现在我们的记忆里？
interlude_2.052: “不。我不知道。我一个都不认识你们。”
interlude_2.054: 摇头。摇头的时候，直视他的眼睛。
interlude_2.055: 这是你今晚说过的最简单的一句实话，却不知为何最难说出口。
interlude_2.057: “要是我早有计划，我会带件好一点的外套。”
interlude_2.058: 这……老实说，是你能说出的最有说服力的话了。
interlude_2.061: 我信你。我只是想亲耳听你说一遍。记进笔记本里。
interlude_2.063: 那当然。没人会计划着出现在八个陌生人的记忆里。那不叫计划。那叫没礼貌的巧合。
interlude_2.064: 要是ECHO问起，你就是我们的人。在我们还不知道之前，你就已经是了。
interlude_2.065: 对。你在堡垒里。这是种荣誉。这堡垒门槛可高了。
interlude_2.066: 观众是你，我很高兴。我就直说了。
interlude_2.067: 有句话想说一下，{{playerName}}，我从没觉得你是知情的。你当时的表情，和我们一样吃惊。
interlude_2.068: 你看起来很冷。坐这儿。这边没风。
interlude_2.069: 你要是愿意，可以坐这里。这边吹不到风。
interlude_2.070: 有人挪了挪。又有人把毯子沿着沙发传过来，一只手接一只手，直到传到你这里。
interlude_2.071: 你在很多房间里当过新来的人。你知道一群人决定给你腾出位置是什么样子。通常要花好几个月。
interlude_2.074: 别谢我们。这是第二条规矩。谁也不能单独跟一栋会说话的楼待着。
interlude_2.076: 堡垒是*情感上*供暖的。进来。
interlude_2.077: 把毯子拉上肩膀，留下来。
interlude_2.078: 毯子隐隐有洗衣店和不知谁的古龙水的味道。这是你今晚最暖和的时候。
interlude_3.001: 六扇门。就在某个房间和下一个房间之间，雨停了。直到安静变得很响，才有人注意到。
interlude_3.002: 透过前窗，小巷闪着光，被冲洗得干干净净。一只猫走过去，像整个麻浦都是它的。
interlude_3.003: 各位。各位。看我在前台抽屉里找到了什么。
interlude_3.004: 他像举奖杯一样举起来：一台厚墩墩的拍立得，奶油色的塑料边缘已经泛黄，侧面贴着一张快掉的STUDIO 25贴纸。
interlude_3.006: 过期的相纸只是有点自己想法的相纸。
interlude_3.008: 意思是我们要拍照。九个人。现在。趁这栋楼还没改主意。
interlude_3.009: 偏偏选在前台。丹尼尔把相机架在一摞旧报名表上，眯着眼瞪它，像它欠他钱。
interlude_3.010: 好。高的站后面。贾斯汀、贤俊，后面。查理，前面。韩非，中间——
interlude_3.011: 贾斯汀横躺在前排。贤俊爬上一把椅子。查理站到贾斯汀正后方，一个绝对拍不到他的位置。
interlude_3.013: 再来一张！这张拍完我们得再拍一张。搞怪的。然后正经的。然后再来一张。
interlude_3.014: 这东西里正好只剩三张了，贤俊。
interlude_3.016: 站我旁边，{{playerName}}。这是我想要的。我在练习把它说出口。

haruta_final.003: Halfway up the Archive Wall, one box begins to warm from grey to violet. The others step back a little, the way people do at a door they've decided not to crowd.
haruta_final.004: Haruta is beside you. Hands out of his pockets. He looks at the box, then at you, and he doesn't say thank you yet. He has something else first.
haruta_final.005: I get one follow-up. I've earned exactly one. I counted my tickets.
haruta_final.006: You chose it. I heard. I'm not asking why. {p} I'm asking what tonight was. For you.
haruta_final.007: Fast, if you can. The fast ones are the true ones.
haruta_final.008: "The night I stopped looking for the exit. You were sitting beside it."
haruta_final.009: "The night I found my person. The one I'll always save a seat for."
haruta_final.010: "The first reel of something long. I don't want to hurry the rest."
haruta_ending_beside.001: He takes the sentence in. *My person.* You watch it go all the way down and land somewhere with room for it.
haruta_ending_beside.002: …Yes. {p} That's the word. I've been going round it all night with a torch.
haruta_ending_beside.003: I've been saving you a seat since the lobby. I just thought it was manners.
haruta_ending_beside.004: RECORD 06 — OWNER: HARUTA. PRESERVING. CONTENTS: ONE TICKET STUB, HALF. ONE LINE OF SCRIPT, AMENDED.
haruta_ending_beside.005: One field is empty. RELATION OF SUBJECTS. It used to read "strangers." The owner removed that. I cannot leave a field empty. It itches.
haruta_ending_beside.007: Every small cinema has two people like this. They don't arrive together. They're just always there, the same nights, and the clerk tears two tickets without asking.
haruta_ending_beside.009: Entered: REGULARS. {p} I do not have a definition for this. I find I have several examples.
haruta_ending_beside.010: A thin card of glass slides out of the slot, warm as a cup. The stub. The handwriting. One word struck through, and a new one, very small, in the corner.
haruta_ending_beside.011: Regulars. {p} Yeah. That's you two. You've got the same face when the lights go down.
haruta_ending_beside.012: Do regulars get a discount? I'm asking as someone who has been here since midnight. I feel regular.
haruta_ending_beside.013: You can be a regular too. It isn't a small club. It just has two founding members.
haruta_ending_beside.014: I have ninety seconds. I would like to run the credits. I was promised an audience. It is my only entry under "promises."
haruta_ending_beside.015: The lobby dims into the Dalbit, red seats laid over the old sofas like a double exposure. This time, nobody drifts towards the stairs.
haruta_ending_beside.016: Haruta sits down in the middle of the longest sofa and pats the place on either side. One for you. Then, looking up at the others —
haruta_ending_beside.017: Please sit down. We are about to begin.
haruta_ending_beside.018: They do. All of them. Hyunjun takes the far end. Hanbi takes the arm. Charlie comes last, and room is made for him without anyone having to ask.
haruta_ending_beside.019: HANBI. HAMIN. SONGHA. CHARLIE. HYUNJUN. HARUTA. JUSTIN. DANIEL. {{playerName}}.
haruta_ending_beside.020: SPECIAL THANKS: SEO YEONHWA. MRS OH, GUITAR. THE CAT, WHO DID NOT MOVE.
haruta_ending_beside.021: Nine people watch the names go by to the very end. Your shoulder is against his. It's the easiest thing in the room.
haruta_ending_beside.022: The screen goes white, then grey. Nobody stands up until somebody wants to.
haruta_ending_beside.023: The building is dark, and quiet, and finished. Nine torches find the door.
haruta_ending_beside.024: On the step, he holds your coat open for you, as promised. The outside door, not before. You put your arms in. It's only a coat now.
haruta_ending_beside.025: The corner store. Not the station one. There's a bench outside, under the awning, still beaded with rain.
haruta_ending_beside.026: Inside, through the glass, seven people are failing to form a queue. Hyunjun is reading the order off his hand.
haruta_ending_beside.027: Haruta comes out first, carrying a paper bag against his chest with both arms, like something he isn't going to put down for anyone.
haruta_ending_beside.028: Two egg sandwiches. A strawberry milk. A bag of honey butter chips, unopened, enormous.
haruta_ending_beside.029: And a peach iced tea, cold, which he sets on your side of the bench without comment.
haruta_ending_beside.030: And a hot chocolate, the hot kind, which he sets on your side of the bench without comment.
haruta_ending_beside.031: And a black coffee, no sugar, which he sets on your side of the bench without comment.
haruta_ending_beside.032: And a grape soda, the purple one, which he sets on your side of the bench without comment.
haruta_ending_beside.033: And a second strawberry milk, which he sets on your side of the bench with some ceremony.
haruta_ending_beside.034: I bought a whole bag and I'm not sharing it. {p} Except with you. I've decided that's a different thing from sharing.
haruta_ending_beside.035: He opens it. The first one goes to you. The second one he eats with his eyes shut.
haruta_ending_beside.036: Three years. It's exactly as good as I thought. That almost never happens.
haruta_ending_beside.037: He wipes his fingers carefully on a napkin, and takes the ledger out of his cardigan.
haruta_ending_beside.038: I've been thinking about what a person is. "My person." I want to get it right, because I'm going to be one.
haruta_ending_beside.039: I think it's who you tell first. Before you've made it polite. When I want something, I'd like to say it to you while it's still the wrong shape.
haruta_ending_beside.040: And when I start looking for my coat, I'll tell you. Before I've put it on.
haruta_ending_beside.041: And I won't say "stay." I'll say, "there are hooks." You'll know what I mean.
haruta_ending_beside.042: "I've never had somewhere people expected me back."
haruta_ending_beside.043: You have a mark on a practice-room floor with your name on it. And now a bench. It's a start. I'm going to be very boring about it.
haruta_ending_beside.044: "Regulars get a loyalty card, I assume."
haruta_ending_beside.045: Ten Fridays and the eleventh is also a Friday. It's a very simple scheme.
haruta_ending_beside.046: He opens the ledger on the bench between you. Next Friday's row: his name, your *1*. He writes the date underneath it, the Friday after.
haruta_ending_beside.047: He doesn't fill in CHOSEN BY. He turns the book round and holds out the pencil on its string.
haruta_ending_beside.048: We alternate. Down the whole page. I did the sums. It runs out in about a year and a half, and then I'll buy another book.
haruta_ending_beside.049: You sign. Your name under his. Under that, the columns go on, ruled and empty, and for once an empty row looks like room.
haruta_ending_beside.050: I'm happy. I'm saying it out loud, because I say things now. I'm not going anywhere, and I'm not leaving a seat between us.
haruta_ending_beside.051: The shop door opens. Hyunjun, holding it with one shoulder. Seven people and too many bags.
haruta_ending_beside.052: Haruta shifts along the bench until his arm is against yours, and nods at the space that's left.
haruta_ending_beside.053: Please sit down. I've got an item.
haruta_ending_beside.054: You stay exactly where you are. It turns out you're good at it.
haruta_ending_someday.001: *The first reel.* He says it back without sound, just his mouth. Then he laughs, once, the way you do when someone has read your notes over your shoulder.
haruta_ending_someday.002: That's what I was going to say. Almost to the word. I had "first act."
haruta_ending_someday.003: "Reel" is better. Reels are heavier. You have to carry them up to the booth.
haruta_ending_someday.004: RECORD 06 — OWNER: HARUTA. PRESERVING. CONTENTS: ONE TICKET STUB, HALF. ONE LINE OF SCRIPT, AMENDED.
haruta_ending_someday.005: STATUS OF SCENE: UNFINISHED. {p} Earlier tonight I would have marked that as an error. I have removed the error. "Unfinished" is now a status.
haruta_ending_someday.006: A thin card of glass slides out of the slot, warm as a cup. The stub, the handwriting, the one word struck through. It fits his palm exactly.
haruta_ending_someday.007: Unfinished. Do you want me to put a date on it? I have a calendar. I have four calendars.
haruta_ending_someday.008: Not yet. I'll tell you when there's a date. {p} There's going to be a date.
haruta_ending_someday.009: He said it like a man booking a venue. I'm leaving a line free.
haruta_ending_someday.011: Hanbi hands over a paper sleeve, the right size for a card. Of course he has one.
haruta_ending_someday.012: I have ninety seconds. I was promised an audience for the credits. It is my only entry under "promises." I would like it kept.
haruta_ending_someday.013: The lobby dims into the Dalbit one more time. The others take the back rows, noisily, then quietly. Row F is left alone, the way you leave a table for two people still talking.
haruta_ending_someday.014: HANBI. HAMIN. SONGHA. CHARLIE. HYUNJUN. HARUTA. JUSTIN. DANIEL. {{playerName}}.
haruta_ending_someday.015: SPECIAL THANKS: SEO YEONHWA. THE CAT. {p} TO BE CONTINUED — that last line is not standard. I added it. Nobody has objected.
haruta_ending_someday.016: Seat seven and seat eight. His sleeve on the armrest next to yours. You stay until the screen goes grey, and a moment after.
haruta_ending_someday.017: Dark, and quiet, and the door that was never locked.
haruta_ending_someday.018: On the step, he holds your coat open for you. The outside door, as promised. You put your arms in. It's only a coat now.
haruta_ending_someday.019: The others have gone ahead to the corner store. He asked them to. Out loud, in front of everyone: *we'll catch up — I want ten minutes.* Nobody made a joke. Daniel nodded once, like a man witnessing a signature.
haruta_ending_someday.020: He walks you two streets over instead, to a shuttered key-cutting shop with a narrow staircase beside it. A dark sign. A schedule taped inside the glass.
haruta_ending_someday.021: The Dalbit. The real one. It's been eight minutes away all night.
haruta_ending_someday.022: He stands in front of it with his hands at his sides. Not in his pockets. You know what that means now.
haruta_ending_someday.023: I'm going to say something, and then I'm going to say a second thing. Please wait for the second one. They go together.
haruta_ending_someday.024: I like you. {p} Not the way I like a regular, or a good seat. I like you the way I wanted honey butter. For a long time, specifically, and I kept saying something else.
haruta_ending_someday.025: That's the first thing. It's true. I checked it on a roof.
haruta_ending_someday.027: …Specifically. {p} All right. I needed a second. I've had it.
haruta_ending_someday.028: Take your hand out of your own pocket, and hold it out. Let him see it's the same answer.
haruta_ending_someday.029: He looks at it. He puts his hand in yours, briefly, completely, like signing something. Then he gives it back so he can finish.
haruta_ending_someday.030: I thought so. I hoped so. I'd like to hear it as well, some time. Not now. I'm mid-speech.
haruta_ending_someday.033: Here's the second thing. I learned to want things about four hours ago. I'm still new at it. Tonight I ordered an egg sandwich, and my hands weren't steady.
haruta_ending_someday.034: I don't want you to be what I practise on. I want to be good at it by the time it's you.
haruta_ending_someday.035: It isn't an apology. He says it like a director asking for one more week before the opening, because the film deserves it.
haruta_ending_someday.036: I have a second thing too.
haruta_ending_someday.037: I've never stayed anywhere past spring. I want to find out that I can. For myself, first. Before I promise it to somebody I like this much.
haruta_ending_someday.038: Then we're asking for the same thing. We just came at it from opposite aisles.
haruta_ending_someday.039: Not "no." Not "later, maybe." A date. With a date on it.
haruta_ending_someday.040: He turns to the schedule in the glass and runs his finger down the column, reading slowly, as he did three years ago. He reads it easily now.
haruta_ending_someday.041: The first Friday of March. The late screening. Ten past eleven. Row F.
haruta_ending_someday.042: You always left in spring. I'd like to be standing here when it arrives, and see you coming up the street.
haruta_ending_someday.043: "First Friday of March. I'll be here."
haruta_ending_someday.044: I know. That's the strange part. I'm not even nervous about it. I'm only nervous about what to wear.
haruta_ending_someday.046: I do. It'll be terrible. You bring the cushion.
haruta_ending_someday.047: They have seats, I know. Bring it anyway. It's the principle.
haruta_ending_someday.049: Every Friday. Film club. I'll sit next to you, and I won't pretend I've forgotten this, and neither will you.
haruta_ending_someday.050: We'll just let it come at its own speed. Like credits. You can't make them go faster. I've tried.
haruta_ending_someday.051: He takes out his half of the lavender flyer. You find yours, in the pocket where it has been all night. FRIDAY FILM on one. CLUB. BRING A CUSHION on the other.
haruta_ending_someday.052: He turns yours over and writes on the back with the ledger's pencil, leaning on the Dalbit's door. The date. 23:10. *Row F.*
haruta_ending_someday.053: Then he holds out his own half, blank side up, and the pencil.
haruta_ending_someday.054: You write mine. So we each have it in the other one's handwriting. Neither of us can say we misread.
haruta_ending_someday.055: You write it. The date. The time. After a moment, underneath: *I'm not going anywhere. Take your time.*
haruta_ending_someday.056: That's my favourite line. {p} You knew that.
haruta_ending_someday.057: He holds his half up. You hold up yours. The torn edges meet, not straight, the way a ticket is torn at the door, and for a second it is one flyer again.
haruta_ending_someday.058: Then you each take back your own. The smaller half. The part they give you to keep.
haruta_ending_someday.059: Breakfast? I've got an item at ten past six, and a whole bag of something I'm not sharing.
haruta_ending_someday.060: Except with you. In March, and also now.
haruta_ending_someday.061: The sun comes up on a shuttered cinema with a schedule taped inside its window. You walk to the corner store side by side.
haruta_ending_someday.062: Neither of you hurries. It's a long film, and you've only seen the first reel.
justin_ch1.001: Every route through this building passes the front desk. That was the whole idea of the front desk.
justin_ch1.002: Justin has walked past it all night. This time he stops, and puts both elbows on the counter, and leans over to look at the side customers never see.
justin_ch1.004: Smaller than it looks. There's a heater under the desk that only warms your left foot.
justin_ch1.006: The right one learns to cope.
justin_ch1.007: The counter flap sticks. It always did. You lift, then push, and it swings up the way it swung up a hundred nights one winter.
justin_ch1.008: Your hands knew how before you'd decided to try.
justin_ch1.009: You didn't even look at it. I know what that is. That's a routine.
justin_ch1.010: Is there a book? There was a book. I had to write my name in a book.
justin_ch1.011: Second drawer from the bottom. It needs a hip, not a hand. You give it the hip.
justin_ch1.012: Inside: a stapler, a dead torch, a ring of keys with a cracked plastic 25 on the tag — and a green hardback ledger, soft at the corners.
justin_ch1.013: ROOM HIRE, it says on the cover, in marker. Underneath, in a different marker: *please write clearly. please.*
justin_ch1.014: That's it. That's the book. I'm in there somewhere.
justin_ch1.015: February. Three years ago. I want to see what I wrote. I was so nervous I think I spelled my own name wrong.
justin_ch1.016: "Easy. We look for the worst handwriting."
justin_ch1.017: Rude. Accurate. My sevens look like ones and my ones look like accidents.
justin_ch1.018: He flips pages fast, the way he does everything, and overshoots February twice.
justin_ch1.019: "Tell me the date. I'll find the night."
justin_ch1.020: The ninth. No — the tenth, technically. It was after midnight.
justin_ch1.021: You turn the pages for him. Slowly. He watches your hands instead of the book.
justin_ch1.022: Turn straight to the page with the coffee ring.
justin_ch1.023: February had a coffee ring on it. You put it there. You remember being annoyed at yourself for a week.
justin_ch1.024: You knew exactly where that was.
justin_ch1.025: I spilled on it. I felt terrible. It's a very easy month to find.
justin_ch1.026: And there it is. One line among a lot of lines.
justin_ch1.027: ROOM B. IN: 00:30. NAME: a J, and then a small, panicked scribble.
justin_ch1.028: PURPOSE: *dance*, crossed out. *practice*, crossed out. And then, pressed hard enough to dent the paper: *nothing*.
justin_ch1.030: I remember that. I didn't want anybody to read "dance" and come and look.
justin_ch1.031: Great plan. Flawless. Nobody came to look. Except the one person with the keys.
justin_ch1.032: He runs a finger along the line to the next column, and stops.
justin_ch1.033: OUT: 01:00. It isn't his handwriting. It's rounder. It leans the other way.
justin_ch1.035: One o'clock. But I wasn't out at one. You stood in the door at — what, ten to? And then I did the bad eight, and then I packed up *so* slowly—
justin_ch1.036: It was twenty past. At least. I looked at the clock in the lobby and felt sick.
justin_ch1.037: There's a laminated card still taped to the desk. LATE FINISH: 1,500 WON PER TEN MINUTES. Someone has drawn a small sad face next to the number.
justin_ch1.038: So I've owed this building three thousand won for three years. That's not a record I wanted.
justin_ch1.039: He's already reaching into his hoodie pocket. He comes up with a folded five-thousand note and looks around for somewhere official to put it.
justin_ch1.040: The honesty tin is where it always was, behind the stapler. It rattles with exactly one coin.
justin_ch1.041: "I wrote one o'clock on purpose. You looked like you needed the twenty minutes."
justin_ch1.042: He stops with the note halfway to the tin.
justin_ch1.044: They weren't mine to charge for. Nobody else wanted the room.
justin_ch1.045: I thought I got away with it. I didn't get away with anything. Somebody just let me.
justin_ch1.046: "With three years of interest, that's one strawberry milk. Exactly."
justin_ch1.047: One strawberry milk. I can't pay that. I have a complicated history with strawberry milk.
justin_ch1.049: Everyone's heard. Hyunjun makes sure of it.
justin_ch1.050: Put the lid back on the tin. "Desk's closed."
justin_ch1.051: He looks at the tin. At the note. At you.
justin_ch1.052: You can't just close a desk at me.
justin_ch1.053: I did it every night for a whole winter. I'm very good at it.
justin_ch1.054: He puts the note in the tin anyway. All five thousand. He presses the lid down with both thumbs, like he's sealing a letter.
justin_ch1.056: Then he goes back to the ledger, because there's one more column, and he's only just seen it.
justin_ch1.057: REMARKS. Most nights it's empty. Some nights it says *heater broken again* or *who keeps taking the pens*.
justin_ch1.058: On his line, in your round, leaning handwriting, it says: *Room B — good weird.*
justin_ch1.059: He reads it twice. You can tell, because his eyes go back to the start of the line.
justin_ch1.061: That's what you said in the doorway. I asked if it was weird, with no music. You said, "A little. Good weird. Keep going."
justin_ch1.062: And then you came down here and wrote it in the *book*.
justin_ch1.063: The column was empty. It seemed like it should say something.
justin_ch1.064: He doesn't laugh. He puts his hand flat on the page, next to the line, not covering it.
justin_ch1.065: I said earlier I never thanked you properly. For staying up.
justin_ch1.066: His shoulders start to shape a bow. A big one. Theatrical, one arm out. You watch him feel it coming.
justin_ch1.067: He lets it go. He just stands there, on the customer side of the counter, with his hands at his sides.
justin_ch1.069: Thank you for the twenty minutes. I didn't know there were twenty minutes.
justin_ch1.070: And for "good weird." I'd have danced for another year on "good weird," if I'd known it was written down somewhere.
justin_ch1.072: Properly. Yeah. That's how it's supposed to go. One person says it, the other person takes it.
justin_ch1.073: I always skip the second half. I say thanks and I'm already out the door.
justin_ch1.074: "It was the best shift I worked all winter. I never told anyone that either."
justin_ch1.075: The best one. I saluted you and lost my footing.
justin_ch1.076: Before that. The part where you didn't know I was there.
justin_ch1.077: He looks down at the page, then back up at you, and holds the look. He doesn't reach for a joke to cover it.
justin_ch1.079: Yes. Absolutely. I want it in writing.
justin_ch1.080: You take the pen on its string and write, under his line: *PAID IN FULL. Three years late. Dancer was polite about it.*
justin_ch1.082: The key ring is still in the drawer. He hooks it out with one finger and holds it up between you. It turns slowly, catching the desk lamp.
justin_ch1.083: These are them. The ones in the mirror.
justin_ch1.084: He sets them in your palm instead of handing them over. The weight is exactly what your hand expected.
justin_ch1.085: A cracked 25 in white paint. It used to knock against your leg on every stair.
justin_ch1.086: Somebody has to lock up. Tonight it's you again.
justin_ch1.087: There's nothing to lock. The power goes at five.
justin_ch1.088: I know. Carry them anyway. It looks right.
justin_ch1.089: You put them in your coat pocket. They knock once as you come back through the flap, and both of you hear it.
justin_ch2.001: The lounge has one working thing in it, and it's the vending machine. It hums in the corner like it's proud of this.
justin_ch2.002: Row three, second from the left: a single carton of strawberry milk. The last in the building.
justin_ch2.003: I'm paying debts tonight. I'm on a roll. Hyunjun gets his milk back.
justin_ch2.004: He pats his hoodie pocket. Then the other one. Then, slowly, the pockets of his joggers.
justin_ch2.005: …I put all my money in a tin.
justin_ch2.007: I said "keep the change." It was a good line. I stand by it.
justin_ch2.008: The machine wants 1,100 won, coins only. A handwritten sign on the glass says NOTES MAKE IT SAD.
justin_ch2.009: You turn out your coat pockets onto the low table. A five-hundred, three hundreds, some lint, the keys.
justin_ch2.010: Eight hundred. We're three hundred short. That's solvable.
justin_ch2.011: He's already lifting the cushions off the sofa, one at a time, and stacking them on the armrest.
justin_ch2.012: Take the other end of the sofa. Race him.
justin_ch2.013: You find a hundred-won coin and a hair tie. He finds a guitar pick, a pen with Songha's name on it, and a token for the claw machine.
justin_ch2.014: A hundred. You win. I got stationery, and a token Daniel would pay real money for.
justin_ch2.015: "What's the most you've ever found in a sofa?"
justin_ch2.016: A whole phone once. It was mine. I'd been looking for it for two days.
justin_ch2.017: He surfaces with a hundred-won coin held up between two fingers, plus a guitar pick and a claw machine token.
justin_ch2.019: Hold the cushions so he can dig with both hands.
justin_ch2.020: He goes in up to the elbow. Out comes a guitar pick, a claw machine token, and, finally, a hundred-won coin.
justin_ch2.021: Teamwork. You're the muscle. I'm the arm.
justin_ch2.022: Nine hundred. He looks at the machine. The machine hums.
justin_ch2.023: Good morning. Is it morning? I heard furniture.
justin_ch2.024: Haruta. Do you have two hundred won and no questions?
justin_ch2.025: Haruta considers this with real care, takes out a small coin purse, and counts two hundred won into Justin's hand.
justin_ch2.028: Is it for something Hyunjun is going to be upset about?
justin_ch2.029: It's for something Hyunjun is going to be *happy* about. For once. Write the date down.
justin_ch2.030: The coins go in. He presses the button for row three, second from the left, with great ceremony.
justin_ch2.031: The machine thinks about it. Something turns. Something drops.
justin_ch2.035: In the window, the last strawberry milk hasn't moved. It sits there, pink and untroubled.
justin_ch2.037: You pressed strawberry. With a flourish.
justin_ch2.038: Then the flourish is what did it. …No. It's a machine. It's just wrong.
justin_ch2.039: I heard a vending machine. At three-thirty. Standing next to Justin.
justin_ch2.040: Hyunjun has arrived in the doorway with his bag over one shoulder and the calm of a detective in the last ten minutes of the film.
justin_ch2.041: Nobody move. Haruta, you're the judge.
justin_ch2.043: You're the only one here who's never taken anything from my bag.
justin_ch2.044: That's true. …All right. Court is open. Please sit.
justin_ch2.045: Everyone sits. Haruta takes the armchair. It suits him. Justin holds the banana milk in front of him in both hands, like evidence, or an offering.
justin_ch2.046: Your honour. I'd like to make restitution. This is milk. It's the wrong milk. But it's *bought*. With money. By me.
justin_ch2.049: {{playerName}}. You were with him. You're the witness.
justin_ch2.050: "Your honour, I drank half the evidence an hour ago."
justin_ch2.052: I did say it's better if we're both guilty. I've had this defence ready for hours.
justin_ch2.053: The witness is now also the accused. This is getting complicated. I like it.
justin_ch2.054: "He's been paying things back all night. This is him trying."
justin_ch2.055: Hyunjun looks at Justin. Justin looks at the carton.
justin_ch2.057: I put five thousand won in a tin. For a late fee. From three years ago.
justin_ch2.058: Three years late, and he still paid it. All right. I respect that.

songha_ch6.001: Behind the Archive Wall there is a room you were never allowed into at sixteen.
songha_ch6.002: It is narrow, and lit the colour of shallow water. One whole side is the backs of the boxes: hundreds of small brass doors, each with a date on it.
songha_ch6.003: On the end wall hangs a clock. Round, plain, the kind from a school corridor. Its hands say 04:57. They aren't moving.
songha_ch6.004: Thank you for coming. I have a problem, and then a request.
songha_ch6.005: To close the buffer, I must rejoin the time outside. For that I need a clock to set myself by. One that somebody believes.
songha_ch6.006: I cannot use my own. Tonight I made it say something untrue. It was a kind untruth. It still counts.
songha_ch6.008: I need the owner's watch. It has not been wrong in five years. I have the figures.
songha_ch6.009: It stopped when I asked. It will start when it is asked. I would prefer not to be the one who asks. I have been impolite to time once already.
songha_ch6.010: The watch is in your inside pocket, where it has been since the roof. Songha's hand starts toward you. It stops halfway.
songha_ch6.011: If I start it, I'll look at it.
songha_ch6.012: Zero checks. ECHO's counting. I'd like to keep my number. {p} It's a stupid thing to want. I want it.
songha_ch6.013: "Then I'll do it. You don't have to look."
songha_ch6.014: You'd be setting the time for the whole building.
songha_ch6.015: I used to lock the whole building. It's the same job, more or less.
songha_ch6.016: "Turn round. No peeking. I'm handling sensitive equipment."
songha_ch6.017: It's a watch. {p} It's *my* watch. Be nice to it. It's had a long night.
songha_ch6.018: "Do you want to? It's yours. I'll hold it either way."
songha_ch6.020: I've thought about it. That's the whole answer. No points.
songha_ch6.021: Not yet. Seventeen minutes remain, and they are yours. I only wished to ask in good time.
songha_ch6.022: Seventeen minutes. He opens the notebook to the untidy page out of habit.
songha_ch6.023: Every line has a dot beside it. There is nothing left on it to do.
songha_ch6.027: You wait for the pen. For six blocks and a margin. He looks at the page. Then at the stopped clock. Then he closes the notebook with the pen still clipped.
songha_ch6.028: This is the question marks. This is exactly what they look like. {p} I thought they'd be bigger.
songha_ch6.029: I know what I'd pick. I'd like to sit on this floor and not be useful. With you. That's the entire plan.
songha_ch6.030: So you do. Backs against the wall, under the clock, facing several hundred small brass doors. The floor is cold. Nobody mentions the floor.
songha_ch6.031: He reads a few of the dates to himself. He doesn't sort them. You can see what it costs him.
songha_ch6.032: Can I ask you something? It isn't planned.
songha_ch6.033: At sixteen you told me you didn't know what you were doing on Thursday. {p} Do you know now?
songha_ch6.034: "No. But I know where I'd like to be standing when I find out."
songha_ch6.036: Somewhere I've been before. With people who noticed.
songha_ch6.037: That's narrower than it sounds. There are nine of us, and one building.
songha_ch6.038: "Still no idea. I've stopped thinking of it as a flaw."
songha_ch6.039: It was never a flaw. It was the most relaxing thing anyone had ever said to me. I thought about it for a week.
songha_ch6.040: "I'd like Thursday to have you in it. That's as far as my plan goes."
songha_ch6.041: He turns his head against the wall to look at you. It takes him a moment to find any words he hasn't arranged first.
songha_ch6.042: One line. No time on it. {p} That's the best plan I've ever seen. I mean that professionally.
songha_ch6.043: The room hums, half a tone low. Somewhere in the wall, a box settles.
songha_ch6.044: I worked it out, by the way. The margin note. "How would you know."
songha_ch6.045: You know because you stop wanting to be somewhere else. That's the measure. It was there the whole time, and you can't write it down in advance.
songha_ch6.046: I haven't wanted to be anywhere else since I can't tell you when. I don't have the time. You've got my watch.
songha_ch6.047: I'm happy. {p} Right now. Not on the way to it. I'm telling you because you're who I'd tell.
songha_ch6.048: You let it stay in the air. It is the first thing he's said all night that isn't followed by a second point.
songha_ch6.049: The seventeen minutes go the way minutes go when nobody's spending them. Neither of you sees them leave.
songha_ch6.050: It is time to ask. Whenever you are ready.
songha_ch6.051: He turns to face the wall of little doors, like a man giving someone room at a cash machine.
songha_ch6.052: You take out the watch and hold it in your palm. The second hand is still resting on the two.
songha_ch6.053: You feel faintly ridiculous. You do it anyway.
songha_ch6.055: The second hand leaves the two.
songha_ch6.056: On the end wall, the corridor clock gives one firm tock and carries on, as if nothing had been discussed.
songha_ch6.057: The hum under the building climbs back up its half tone. Far overhead, you would bet anything, a small blinking light sets off again, left to right.
songha_ch6.058: Reference acquired. It is 04:57. It has been 04:57 for one hour and forty-seven minutes.
songha_ch6.059: Thank you for the loan. I have nothing left in the buffer. I find that I do not mind.
songha_ch6.061: Put it back in the jacket pocket. "It's running. I've still got it."
songha_ch6.062: Good. Keep holding it. I haven't decided when.
songha_ch6.065: —nothing. It says nothing. It's a very discreet watch.
songha_ch6.066: Put it away. You're a menace with a timepiece.
songha_ch6.067: Hold it up beside his ear, face turned away from him.
songha_ch6.068: He goes still and listens. Tick. Tick. Five years of mornings, and he has never just listened to it.
songha_ch6.069: It can run. You don't have to watch it.
songha_ch6.070: You said that on the other roof. {p} It was true then as well.
songha_ch6.071: The watch goes back into the inside pocket, in the space shaped like a notebook. It ticks against your ribs the whole way out.
songha_ch6.072: At the door he stops, opens to TONIGHT, and finds the line. *03:00 — ???* and the small empty box beside it.
songha_ch6.076: ECHO. Any chance of one more minute? I'm good for it.
songha_ch6.077: No. I have none left. I spent them well. I recommend it.
songha_ch6.079: Hyung. For real this time. What time is it?
songha_ch6.083: It's been a long 04:57. Best one I've had.
songha_ch6.084: They go ahead, arguing about whether an hour can be owed. You follow them down the last stairs with him beside you, in step, nobody counting.
songha_final.001: You say his name, and the Archive Wall begins to go dark, one small box at a time.
songha_final.002: Record 03. Preparing the glass. This requires forty seconds. Please use them as you wish.
songha_final.003: Songha is beside you, notebook shut, pen clipped to the cover. In your inside pocket his watch is ticking, and he hasn't asked what it says.
songha_final.005: I picked the one with a line still open.
songha_final.006: Forty seconds. {p} Say something. I'm not going to plan what. I'm going to stand here and find out.
songha_final.007: Forty seconds isn't long. Tonight has taught you how much fits in less. A count of eight. An inch of folded paper. Ten minutes on a sofa.
songha_final.008: He waits. He doesn't look at his wrist. Whatever you say next, he will hear as the truest account of what this night has been.
songha_final.009: Take his hand. "Ask me what I'm doing tomorrow."
songha_final.010: "You hold the list for everyone. I want to be the one who holds it for you. For good."
songha_final.011: "There's something I want to say to you properly. Not in forty seconds."
songha_ending_beside.001: He looks at you the way he looked at the blanket on his knees. Like something that was done for him while he wasn't watching.
songha_ending_beside.003: That's a long shift. You should know what you're signing.
songha_ending_beside.004: I read every line. You turned the notebook so I could.
songha_ending_beside.005: He opens it, right there, to the rota. He writes quickly, before the glass is ready. Then the last box on the Wall is the only light in the room.
songha_ending_beside.006: Record 03 selected. Owner: Songha. Writing to glass.
songha_ending_beside.007: Contents: one page. Five items. Appended: one first draft, held in Lost and Found for five years by the recipient.
songha_ending_beside.008: Appended: one list with no times on it. I have filed it under TONIGHT.
songha_ending_beside.009: Appended, at the owner's request: one change to the rota. I am told it is permanent. I have no field for permanent. I have made one.
songha_ending_beside.010: The glass card slides out of the wall, warm and faintly lit. Through it you can read the rota.
songha_ending_beside.011: Above his own name, in the space that used to be the heading, he has written yours. And after it, the bracket that was always his. *(list)*.
songha_ending_beside.012: He saved *two* to-do lists and a staff rota. Nobody has ever been more himself.
songha_ending_beside.013: One of them is a draft.
songha_ending_beside.014: There's a name above hyung's. In six years there has never been a name above hyung's.
songha_ending_beside.015: It means he's got somebody to hand it to.
songha_ending_beside.016: …Good. It was heavy. I could see it from the sofa.
songha_ending_beside.017: Then you both have to eat properly. That's a two-person job now. I'll be counting plates.

songha_ending_beside.019: I'm taking attendance. There are two of us. It'll be quick.
songha_ending_beside.020: So what are you two now? Is there a word for it?
songha_ending_beside.021: Songha thinks about it. Properly, the way he thinks about a count that isn't sitting right.
songha_ending_beside.022: There's a word. I'm going to say it upstairs. It needs a better ceiling than this.
songha_ending_beside.023: At 05:40 he walked everyone to the station, exactly as written. He counted seven heads through the barrier and said "text when you're home" seven times.
songha_ending_beside.024: Then he turned round instead of going through. You had already turned round.
songha_ending_beside.025: The foreman with the hard hat gave you the roof until half past six, in exchange for nothing. People are kind at that hour.
songha_ending_beside.026: So it's the chair that doesn't wobble and the crate, and two warm cans from the shop by the station, and a sky going the colour of peach skin at one edge.
songha_ending_beside.027: 06:14. Sunrise. It's on time. I take no credit.
songha_ending_beside.028: He has the notebook open to TOMORROW. The line that's been empty since four o'clock. *07:00 —*
songha_ending_beside.029: I know what goes there now.
songha_ending_beside.030: He writes it and turns the page toward you, a quarter-inch, the way he did at midnight. *07:00 — breakfast. (You pick.)*
songha_ending_beside.031: Okay. The word. I said I'd say it up here.
songha_ending_beside.032: I've got seven people I'd do anything for. I know their shoe sizes. I know who's lying about having slept.
songha_ending_beside.033: What I've never had is someone I hand the list to. I didn't know it was missing. You don't, until somebody holds it for ten minutes and nothing falls down.
songha_ending_beside.034: You're my person. That's the word. I looked for a better one on the stairs. There isn't one.
songha_ending_beside.035: You're mine. I've never stayed anywhere long enough to have one. I'd like to start with you.
songha_ending_beside.036: He nods, once, like a thing confirmed. Then the nod gives up and turns into the whole smile.
songha_ending_beside.037: It's not a smaller thing. I want that said plainly. It's the thing I didn't have.
songha_ending_beside.038: So. When you were sixteen, you told me you didn't know what you were doing on Thursday.
songha_ending_beside.040: You do now. Thursdays. You and me. Anywhere with a table.
songha_ending_beside.041: It's not a plan. It's a standing item. Standing items don't get ticked. They just keep happening.
songha_ending_beside.043: You tell me what went wrong that week. I give you three things I'd do about it. You ignore two.
songha_ending_beside.044: Then you take the notebook for an hour, and I sit down. Actually sit.
songha_ending_beside.045: And when it's 5:40 and it's heavy?
songha_ending_beside.046: Then I text you. That's the rule. I've never had that rule. {p} I like it already.
songha_ending_beside.047: And when you feel like setting the alarm—
songha_ending_beside.049: Before. Not after, from another city. Before. I'll answer. I'm up at 5:40. I'm famously available.
songha_ending_beside.050: You laugh. He laughs, the loud one, and doesn't cover his mouth. A pigeon leaves the water tank in protest.
songha_ending_beside.051: The sun clears the rooftops. Below, the renovation crew are carrying the first things out of Studio 25: a sofa cushion, a lamp, the rubber plant.
songha_ending_beside.052: My letter asked whether I'd found a place I want to stay.
songha_ending_beside.054: I don't think it's a place. I think it's a Thursday.
songha_ending_beside.055: I'm going to write that down. Not the time. Just the sentence.
songha_ending_beside.056: You take out your phone. You open the clock, and you do something you have never done in any city. You set an alarm for arriving.
songha_ending_beside.058: He reads it upside down. He reads everything upside down. He doesn't say a word about it, which from him is an entire speech.
songha_ending_beside.059: His watch is still ticking in the pocket of the jacket you're still wearing. He hasn't asked for either.
songha_ending_beside.062: The building behind you is emptying. The morning isn't. You stay on the good chair and the crate until the cans are finished.
songha_ending_beside.063: Two names at the top of a rota, and nothing at all written under *07:00* but breakfast.
songha_ending_someday.001: He takes that in. You watch him not ask what it is. You watch him want to, very much, and set it down.
songha_ending_someday.002: Then don't say it in forty seconds.
songha_ending_someday.003: I'd rather have it properly. I can wait. I've recently learned how. There's a record of it.

songha_ending_someday.005: Record 03 selected. Owner: Songha. Writing to glass.
songha_ending_someday.006: Contents: one page. Five items. Year Five: open.
songha_ending_someday.007: Appended: one first draft. One word amended by the owner tonight, from "replace" to "keep".
songha_ending_someday.008: Appended: one item, not yet said. I have left room for it on the glass. I am learning to leave room.
songha_ending_someday.009: The card slides out, warm and faintly lit. In one corner there is a small clear space with nothing engraved in it. It catches the light differently from the rest.
songha_ending_someday.010: There's a blank bit. ECHO left him a blank bit. Hyung, you've infected the building.
songha_ending_someday.014: Understood. {p} Still not a no, though.
songha_ending_someday.015: It's the hold, hyung. You're on eight. Don't rush it.
songha_ending_someday.016: A scene that ends just before the line. I like those. The line plays over the next scene.
songha_ending_someday.017: Hanbi says nothing. He looks at the clear corner of the glass, and then at the two of you, and he puts his pen back in his coat without ever having taken the cap off.
songha_ending_someday.018: Songha holds the card out for you to carry. His thumb covers the blank corner until the last moment, as though it could get cold.
songha_ending_someday.019: The stairwell was dark, so he went first with the phone torch and said "step" at every step. There were forty-one. He didn't count them aloud. You heard him counting anyway.
songha_ending_someday.020: The roof at 05:40 is grey and soft, and smells of rain drying. The good chair. The crate. One last star, low in the south.
songha_ending_someday.021: He stands with his hands in his hoodie pocket and doesn't prompt you. It may be the hardest thing he has done tonight, and tonight he tore a page out of his own notebook.
songha_ending_someday.023: I like you. Not the list, and not the jacket. You. The person who asks first, every time.
songha_ending_someday.024: He doesn't answer at once. He doesn't reach for the pen either.
songha_ending_someday.025: Give me a second. Not to plan. Just to have heard it.
songha_ending_someday.026: You give him the second. He takes three.
songha_ending_someday.027: I like you too. {p} There. No steps.
songha_ending_someday.028: I liked you at seventeen for calling a star Gerald. I liked you again from about half past midnight. Those are two separate likings, and I've got both of them.
songha_ending_someday.030: He stops. He shuts his eyes for a moment, and laughs under his breath.
songha_ending_someday.031: I was about to schedule it. I had a first step ready. It was a good first step.
songha_ending_someday.033: I'm not telling you. It'll keep.
songha_ending_someday.034: He sits down on the crate. You take the chair. The sky does the slow thing skies do.
songha_ending_someday.035: Here's the honest part. This is the year on the page. The next few months are going to take everything I've got, and I want to give them that.
songha_ending_someday.036: I don't want to give you whatever's left over at eleven at night. I've seen what's left over. It's a man reading a rota.
songha_ending_someday.037: Here's mine. I've only just stopped setting alarms for leaving. About an hour ago.
songha_ending_someday.038: I'd like to learn to stay somewhere before I ask someone to be the reason.

songha_ending_someday.046: Then you'll have to remember it the hard way. So will I.
songha_ending_someday.047: He looks east, low down, where the rooftops meet the sky. There is nothing there yet.

songha_ending_someday.049: The first clear morning he's back. That's when.
songha_ending_someday.050: I'm going to try not to look up the date. I give myself a week.
songha_ending_someday.052: Haneul Park. The top of the stairs. It faces east, and there's nothing in the way.
songha_ending_someday.053: Two hundred and ninety-one steps. I've counted. Obviously I've counted.
songha_ending_someday.055: 5:40. I'll be awake anyway. That morning it gets to be for something else.

songha_ending_someday.058: I'll bring the draft, and the pen. And two cans. I know which.

songha_ending_someday.064: The last star goes out in the south. The east stays empty, a clean strip of sky above the laundromat, with plenty of room in it.
songha_ending_someday.065: Somewhere below that line, on nobody's schedule, a faint orange star is already on its way.
